title: We Buy Houses in Portsmouth, VA | Sell Fast for Cash
description: We buy houses in Portsmouth, VA for cash, as-is. Local REALTOR® Chris Jenkins makes honest no-obligation offers with no repairs, showings or listing fees.
h1: We Buy Houses in Portsmouth, VA: Sell Your House Fast for Cash
lede: If you want to sell a Portsmouth house quickly and without repairs, I will make you a straight cash offer and tell you honestly when listing would net you more.
tldr: Chris Jenkins, a licensed Virginia REALTOR® with Better Homes and Gardens Real Estate – Native American Group, buys Portsmouth houses for cash, as-is. Each offer comes from nearby closed sales and the condition of the house.
service_name: Cash home buying in Portsmouth, Virginia
card: Cash offers on Portsmouth houses, as-is, on your timeline.

sections.h2: Selling Your Portsmouth House for Cash
sections.html:
Portsmouth is a compact city across the Elizabeth River from Norfolk, with historic Olde Towne, older neighborhoods and newer pockets. Values vary block to block, so a cash offer has to be built from sales near your address.

I have not published Portsmouth neighborhood statistics on this site yet, so I will not quote a median. Send your address and I will pull the nearby closed sales from REIN MLS and show you the numbers.

sections.h2: Shipyard and Naval Medical Center Households
sections.html: Portsmouth is home to Norfolk Naval Shipyard and Naval Medical Center Portsmouth. Many sellers here are on orders or changing jobs at the yard. Tell me your dates and I will say honestly whether a direct sale, listing or rental fits. Read VA loan entitlement and PCS moves first.

sections.h2: Older Homes, Vacant Houses and Landlords
sections.html:
Older houses often carry deferred maintenance, and vacant ones cost money every month. If yours is either, selling as-is can end the carrying costs.

Virginia lets localities set up rental inspection districts. Ask the city what applies to your address, then tell me about the lease and condition if you own a rental.

sections.h2: Inherited Houses and Probate in Portsmouth
sections.html: Probate is handled by the circuit court clerk in the city where the person lived, which for a Portsmouth resident is the Portsmouth Circuit Court clerk. Read how to sell an inherited house and see a Virginia attorney.

sections.h2: Flood Zones and Disclosure in Portsmouth
sections.html: Portsmouth sits on the water, so check your flood zone before selling. Selling as-is does not remove disclosure duties. See the DPOR disclosure statement and read whether you need flood insurance.

faqs: Do you buy Portsmouth houses in any condition?
I look at houses in many conditions, including ones that need major work. Tell me what you know and I will give an honest answer.
How do you decide what to offer on a Portsmouth house?

I pull closed sales near your address from REIN MLS, subtract the repairs and updates the house needs and the cost and risk of holding and reselling it, and show you the math. A cash offer is generally below what a fully prepared house could get on the open market.
I work at the shipyard or the medical center. Can you work around my timeline?
Yes. Tell me your date and what is owed on the house, and I will say honestly whether a direct sale or listing fits.
Can I sell a Portsmouth rental with a tenant?
Often, yes. Tenants have rights under their lease and Virginia law, so I will review the lease with you and, where needed, your attorney.
Who can sell an inherited Portsmouth house?
Generally the executor or administrator, after qualifying with the circuit court clerk. A Virginia attorney can confirm the steps.
In most cases you can sell until the foreclosure sale takes place. Read this guide.
Do I pay a Realtor commission if I sell to you in Portsmouth?

On a direct sale there is no listing commission. Closing costs and taxes still apply, and I will go over them with you before you decide. I will also tell you honestly what listing would likely net you.
How do I know this is not a scam?
Ask who the actual buyer is, ask for proof of funds, get the offer in writing, close through a title company or attorney and check any license with the Virginia DPOR.
